name: The Lulboom of Megen
age_estimate: roughly 86 to 96 years, from the register's planting band of 1930-1940

location.address: Megen, on a street just outside the historic centre

access: Free, on a public street, open at all times.
verify_notes: LRMB register nr 1696841, registered name 'Zilverlinde als Lulboom' (silver lime, known locally as the Lulboom). Planting band 1930-1940, age 86-96 years. Owner category gemeente, setting weg (street). Register's own history: in 1937 Princess Juliana (later Queen) married Prince Bernhard, and to mark it the small town of Megen planted a 'koningslinde' (king's lime) at a prominent spot just outside its historic core. Over the years it became a meeting place for young and old; people sitting on the bench beside it enjoying the view and a chat is how it got the name 'lulboom' (roughly, 'chinwag tree' or 'gab tree' in local dialect, a nickname from casual conversation at the spot, not a species term). This is a genuinely good, specific local story tied to a real royal-wedding commemorative planting, distinct from the separate nearby 'Lulboom' entry (register nr 1681077, a few metres away, which is NOT this tree and should not be conflated with it). The register is the ONE source found this pass; no girth or height recorded.
